html:
A boom in land and share prices in Japan from 1986 to 1991, followed by a long crash. The Japanese call it the bubble economy.

After the Plaza Accord of 1985 pushed up the yen, the Bank of Japan cut interest rates to protect exporters. Cheap credit flowed into property and shares. Banks lent against land at ever higher values, and companies bought buildings and art abroad. The Nikkei index on the Tokyo Stock Exchange peaked at the end of 1989.

The central bank then raised rates, and prices fell. Shares lost more than half their value within a few years, and land prices kept falling for over a decade. Banks were left with bad loans they hid rather than wrote off, which slowed recovery. The years of weak growth that followed are called the Lost Decades. The Nikkei did not pass its 1989 peak until 2024.

It ended the image of Japan as the economy about to overtake the United States.
sum: A boom in land and share prices in Japan from 1986 to 1991, followed by a long crash. The Japanese call it the bubble economy.
